scenes.text: Every software project needs more than code. It also needs a clear, shared way of working. Project Orchestrator brings that structure into your repository. It gives GitHub Copilot the instructions, prompts, agents, and reusable skills it needs — all installed as one verified foundation.

There are two parts. First, a registry-free command-line installer can create a new workspace, or carefully adopt an existing one. It runs entirely on the tools built into Node.js. Then, a catalog of forty-four governed skills gives Copilot focused capabilities — with clear inputs, outputs, checks, approval gates, and stop conditions.

Begin by cloning the repository, then run the verify command. You will need Node.js version twenty-two, twenty-four, or twenty-six. Verification makes sure the distribution is complete. It also checks that the skill contracts, schemas, dependencies, and ownership claims all agree — before you use the installer anywhere else.

When you are starting fresh, run create-project. Give the project a name and destination. Then choose a conformance profile and identify the technology stack. The durable profile is the default. You will get a standalone, governed workspace — with source and test boundaries, editor settings, continuous integration wiring, and the complete skill catalog. Your application code remains yours to build.

For an existing repository, adoption happens in two stages. Start with a dry run. The plan shows the technologies it found, the files it would create, standards that are already covered, and any blocking conflicts. Review that plan first. Then apply it with explicit risk acceptance. Your project instructions and application code stay in place, while each managed change is journaled and verified.

Once you are inside Visual Studio Code, begin with project start. Project blueprint captures the agreed purpose, technology stack, delivery target, quality requirements, assumptions, and acceptance criteria. From there, specialized skills can help plan, implement, review, test, and document the work. Project validate and project status keep blocked, stale, or pending work visible.

Agent Builder now supports two deliberate paths. Guided mode starts from supplied requirements. Autonomous research gathers bounded evidence before proposing a blueprint. Both validate a least-privilege local agent, require review, and install transactionally. Publication intent uses blueprint schema two point two and plan schema one point one, while the updated command line, runtime, schemas, and tests propagate into newly generated projects.

Publication is a governed handoff, not an automatic side effect. A Foundry endpoint is managed with its agent. Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams distribution requires its own Activity Protocol and Bot Service prerequisites. ChatGPT integration is indirect, through a separately governed Custom GPT HTTPS and OpenAPI Action. Agent Builder records the plan, but it creates none of those external resources.

Autonomy does not erase consent. Six consequential actions always remain approval-gated: purchases, bookings, messages, account-security changes, sensitive disclosures, and destructive actions. Publication metadata stays in the reviewed plan and never enters the installed agent instructions, so distribution intent cannot trigger runtime behavior.

The milestone is backed by current evidence: one hundred twenty-four tests passed with one platform-specific skip, all forty-four skills were verified, two hundred six files passed the security scan, and one hundred fifty-eight release files passed checksum verification. Azure Government readiness fails closed when current evidence is unknown. The candidate is still unsigned, and P4 release assurance remains blocked.

That is Project Orchestrator version one point one point one — a repeatable way to make both engineering workflows and agent creation part of the repository itself. Verify the distribution. Provision a workspace. Build governed agents. Then let each important action leave evidence that people and automation can inspect.
